chapter: Savoy days, the Concord and business
title: Tiny Bradshaw, Lucky Millinder and manager Charlie Buchanan
summary: He recalls other Savoy bandleaders and the manager who booked the bands.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Tiny Bradshaw. He was up the Savoy quite a few times. This was before Chick Webb and Benny Goodman had, they started having those, you know, good Swing sessions up there.
He was, I didn't know Tiny too well. But, I had a lot of fun with him. I think he was a drummer. I'm not sure. But, he directed.
Yeah. I never saw him play anything. He used to have the baton. I never knew what he played.

I think, I think I heard someone say something about the drummer, but I'm not sure. But, he used to have a very good band. He used to go and Lucky Millinder, very good out there in front of directing. (Inaudible) remind me of each other.
But Savoy days, during those days, were some years. Charlie Buchanan was the manager. I'm pretty sure you heard of him. But, he brought those bands in there and the boys,
the bands always waited until their next turn to come to the Savoy Ballroom, you know, cause that was some name then.
